background.title: Background
background.copy: Aileen Wuornos, a homeless sex worker, was convicted of murdering six men in Florida between 1989 and 1990. A survivor of relentless abuse, she maintained that each killing was self-defense.

howTo.title: How to use this kiosk
steps: Review key excerpts from the trial and defense strategy.
Track mitigating factors: trauma, police pressure, psychiatric findings.
Enter your verdict and compare it with previous visitors.

charges.title: Charges & complaints
charges.intro: State filings enumerate six separate homicides plus robberies tied to the victims' missing property. Read the language prosecutors used to frame Wuornos as a predator.

items.label: Capital murder counts
items.title: Mallory, Spears, & Carskaddon
items.summary: Indictments describe her flagging down drivers, pulling the .22 first, and stripping valuables before leaving them roadside.

facts.label: Shots
facts.text: Autopsies cite tight point-blank clusters to the chest and head, matching ambush executions.

facts.label: Evidence
facts.text: Latex gloves, rope, and the pistol seized from her locker tie directly to the three scenes.

facts.label: Pattern
facts.text: Complaints list the same method: lure, disarm, rob, and dump the bodies in ditches.

items.label: Theft & fraud complaints
items.title: Burress & Humphreys families
items.summary: Families filed fraud complaints once pawn slips, forged signatures, and missing ID cards surfaced within days of each disappearance.

facts.label: Pawn trail
facts.text: Burress' camera, badge, and jewelry were pawned under aliases with her thumbprint on the ticket.

facts.label: Cards
facts.text: Motel folios and gas receipts show Humphreys' credit cards used by Wuornos hours after he vanished.

facts.label: Forgery
facts.text: Bank investigators testified signatures on checks and DMV forms matched her handwriting, not the victims'.

items.label: Aggravating petitions
items.title: Peter Siems disappearance
items.summary: Moore and Siems' sister swore that taped confessions described "leaving no witnesses" during robbery runs.

facts.label: Confession
facts.text: Moore told investigators Wuornos bragged about shooting him twice "so he couldn't talk."

facts.label: Car
facts.text: His Oldsmobile was found abandoned and wiped down, while her palm print sat on the door glass.

facts.label: Aftermath
facts.text: Bartenders reported she flashed new cash the same night, reinforcing the robbery motive.

evidenceData.title: Documented Childhood Abuse
evidenceData.summary: Social workers and family interviews describe sustained abuse from early childhood.
details: Placed with alcoholic grandparents at age four, Wuornos reported beatings, rapes, and a group assault at fourteen logged in a 1970 report.
Teachers described a teenager sleeping in school hallways and exchanging sex for food and clothing.
In 1976 a court-appointed psychiatrist concluded she had severe post-traumatic stress and dissociative symptoms rooted in chronic trauma.
The defense noted that several male accusers carried prior convictions for violence or sexual assault.
evidenceData.quote: She never had a safe place. Every man she met wanted to buy or take her body.

evidenceData.title: Forensic Evidence & Stolen Items
evidenceData.summary: State experts outlined the physical evidence linking Wuornos to each victim.
details: A .22 caliber revolver recovered from a storage locker she rented fired cartridges that matched scenes from all six homicides.
Her fingerprints were found inside multiple victims' vehicles along with spent casings wrapped in a towel traced to her camp.
Pawn slips showed she sold a camera, tools, and jewelry within hours of the murders along with photocopies of the victims' IDs.
Highway patrol recovered the purse of Peter Siems from a dumpster near a bar where Wuornos was witnessed celebrating with cash.
evidenceData.quote: The ballistic chain is uninterrupted: one weapon, six murders, and every artifact flowed back to the defendant.
evidenceData.attribution: FDLE (Florida Department of Law Enforcement) ballistics report - Exhibit 137

evidenceData.title: Tyra Moore's Statement
evidenceData.summary: Moore detailed the confessions that convinced jurors it was planned robbery turned murder.
details: Moore told jurors Wuornos admitted pulling the gun first when clients resisted giving up cash or vehicles.
She described plotting which truckers seemed most isolated and rehearsing matching cover stories.
Phone recordings captured Wuornos begging Moore to stick to the self-defense version, then admitting she shot 'to leave no witnesses'.
Prosecutors argued Moore had nothing to gain by lying after receiving immunity for unrelated fraud charges.
evidenceData.quote: She said the only way out was to take what they had and make sure they couldn't follow.

evidenceData.title: Psychiatric Evaluations
evidenceData.summary: Mental health assessments prepared before and during the trial.
details: Three forensic psychiatrists found borderline personality disorder compounded by complex PTSD.
Projective tests revealed dissociative episodes, extreme hypervigilance, and a distorted perception of male danger.
During interviews she described flashbacks in which clients' faces blurred with those of past abusers.
Defense experts argued that in crisis she could no longer separate actual threats from anticipated ones.
evidenceData.quote: Her psyche is that of a survivor in permanent war, convinced that killing was the only exit.
evidenceData.attribution: Dr. L. Morgan, psychiatric expert - transcript page 572

evidenceData.title: Exploitation and Pimps
evidenceData.summary: Clips show how violent intermediaries controlled Wuornos' work.
details: Former sex workers said multiple pimps took up to seventy percent of her earnings and beat her when she refused clients.
A bar owner admitted hiding assaults committed by regulars to avoid alienating local police.
A neighbor testified Wuornos returned home covered in bruises, hiding them under long sleeves even in summer.
The defense stressed she feared retaliation too much to report the violence she endured.
evidenceData.quote: She told herself: if I refuse, I die. If I accept, I might die anyway.
evidenceData.attribution: T. Daniels, former colleague - investigative documentary

evidenceData.title: Questionable Police Interview
evidenceData.summary: Recorded sequence showing pressure applied during the initial confession.
details: Investigators held her ten hours without a lawyer, promising mercy if she implicated ex-partner Tyra Moore.
Officers offered sodas and cigarettes while repeating that death row was inevitable without cooperation.
The transcript shows she echoed narratives suggested by police, including premeditated robbery.
The defense argues she confessed to protect Moore from prosecution.
evidenceData.quote: I'll say whatever you want, just let Tyra go.

evidenceData.title: Sentencing Phase
evidenceData.summary: Closing arguments and legal questions from the penalty phase.
details: The prosecutor emphasized premeditation and multiple victims to justify capital punishment.
The defense cited the absence of social and medical support plus recommendations for secure psychiatric commitment.
The judge limited how much prior abuse could be considered, ruling it was not a sufficient legal excuse.
Two jurors hesitated about a death sentence but followed the majority after three hours of deliberation.
evidenceData.quote: We weighed the statute, but who weighs the suffering she carried?
evidenceData.attribution: Juror note preserved in the defense archives
